item.title: BMG Acquires Jet’s Music Publishing Interests
item.description:
[Upbeat music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: "Welcome to the latest music news. We've got an exciting update from Down Under. Australian rock band Jet has just made a significant deal with BMG, the independent music company. Let's dive in.
BMG has acquired the music publishing interests of three of Jet's original members: Nic Cester, Cam Muncey, and Mark Wilson. This expands on their existing long-term relationship and follows the purchase of Jet's recordings catalog in 2023.
Nic Cester, the band's frontman, says they're excited to extend their partnership with BMG, allowing their songs to reach new audiences. And with a career spanning over two decades, Jet has certainly made their mark. Formed in the late 1990s, they rose to fame in the early 2000s, alongside other notable Australian bands like The Vines and Avalanches.
Jet's discography includes three studio albums, all of which cracked the top 40 on the Billboard 200. Their debut album, Get Born, is a standout, certified nine-times platinum in Australia and featuring hits like 'Are You Gonna Be My Girl', 'Look What You've Done', and 'Cold Hard Bitch'.
According to BMG, Jet's record sales have topped 6.5 million worldwide. The band was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame in 2023 and continues to tour internationally. Heath Johns, president of BMG in Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, praises Jet as one of the most recognizable Australian bands globally, with an enduring legacy that will continue to inspire new generations of rock 'n' roll fans.
That's the latest from the music world. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next update."
[Upbeat music fades back in]
